title: Chapter XVI

writingPrompts.label: AP

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman

writingPrompts.label: College Sophomore

writingPrompts.label: College Junior

writingPrompts.label: College Senior

segments.script: Today's words: misleads — leads into a wrong idea; disgracing — bringing shame on; reverting — going back (to a subject); unguarded — frank; careless about hiding feelings; godfather — any man who serves as a sponsor for a child at baptism. “misleads”: Origin of “mislead”: Middle English mysleden; earlier Old English mislǣdan (“to mislead”). “disgracing”: Origin of “disgrace”: Middle French disgracier.

words.sentence: Collins,” said she, “speaks highly both of Lady Catherine and her daughter; but from some particulars that he has related of her ladyship, I suspect his gratitude misleads him, and that in spite of her being his patroness, she is an arrogant, conceited woman.”
His behaviour to myself has been scandalous; but I verily believe I could forgive him anything and everything, rather than his disappointing the hopes and disgracing the memory of his father.”
After many pauses and many trials of other subjects, Elizabeth could not help reverting once more to the first, and saying—
I have a warm, unguarded temper, and I may perhaps have sometimes spoken my opinion of him, and to him, too freely.

segments.script: A 'living' was a church post with income controlled by a patron. Readers learn alongside Elizabeth that a confident story is not proof—central to the theme of prejudice. Characterization: Wickham tells Elizabeth that Darcy cheated him of a promised living; he says he will never expose Darcy, then does exactly that. Irony: Wickham claims discretion while gossiping to a near stranger. Watch for rank and condescension: Rank is displayed and enforced, above all at Rosings by Lady Catherine; Elizabeth refuses to be cowed. In this chapter: “have supposed himself in the small summer breakfast parlour at Rosings; a comparison that did not at first convey much gratification; but” (Chapter XVI, paragraph 2).
